> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **142** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 0253192f760b37b5d3da4c4f845aee1c239e6ec2` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `a9b55a3bca35e2238b09cdd6ab05a3c4713d55f5` — the merge of head `02620920532ca719a86343a3c643bb324898843e` into base `0253192f760b37b5d3da4c4f845aee1c239e6ec2`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin a9b55a3bca35e2238b09cdd6ab05a3c4713d55f5 && git checkout a9b55a3bca35e2238b09cdd6ab05a3c4713d55f5
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 0253192f760b37b5d3da4c4f845aee1c239e6ec2 02620920532ca719a86343a3c643bb324898843e && git checkout -B drift-repro 0253192f760b37b5d3da4c4f845aee1c239e6ec2 && git merge --no-ff 02620920532ca719a86343a3c643bb324898843e

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 0253192f760b37b5d3da4c4f845aee1c239e6ec2
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 0253192f760b37b5d3da4c4f845aee1c239e6ec2` → pass the list as

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `02620920532ca719a86343a3c643bb324898843e`
Local-runs: none

Rendered by an isolated reviewer subagent of the seat in `Reviewed-by`, which adopts it.

Inputs, read at 2026-10-11T18:59Z: card #22792 (its body and every comment, the seat's ACCEPT `6112454274` read as data and re-judged); ruling A `6107185582` on #22795 and ruling C `6110031776` on #22851; PR #22847 (body, the 11-file list, the net diff of the head against `origin/main`, whose merge base `0253192f7` equals the PR's base); the 46 check-runs on the head (latest per name: none failed, 4 skipped as path-scheduled or opt-in jobs, and every one of the seven required contexts `success`). The card is `security`: classes and positions only below.

### ① Derived judgments

- **Accept-set of `POST /api/v1/security/explain`: unchanged — right.** No request key is added or removed; `recordId` and `recordIds` keep their validation; the batch form answers each id through the singular service call (the dogfood pin holds it for a self-asker and for an administrator). No route, query parameter or body field moves anywhere in the diff.
- **Public surface of `@objectstack/plugin-security`: unchanged — right.** `src/index.ts` is untouched (`explainAccess`, `buildContextForUser`, `ExplainEngineDeps`, `ExplainInput`); `explainAccess(deps, input)` keeps its signature and now delegates as a self-explanation; `ExplainEngineDeps.recordAbsentToCaller` and `SecurityPlugin.explainAccessForCaller(request, callerContext?)` are comment-only diffs. The new names (`explainAccessForAsker` and `ExplainAsker` in `explain-engine.ts`; `unreadableUnderCallerRead` in `security-plugin.ts`) are module-internal: the package's `exports` map publishes the single `.` entry and `files` ships `dist` only, so no subpath reaches them — checked on the exports map, not only on the built declaration the dev measured.
- **Published behaviour of `explainAccess` for a direct embedder that wires `recordAbsentToCaller`: a self-explained `read` or `export` of a row the principal's door withholds now answers as a missing record — right, and declared.** It is ruling A sub-ruling 1, and the changeset's "Before" sentence states it.
- **The asker gate — right as ruled.** In `explainOnce` (`explain-engine.ts`), every record-grained explanation first asks the asker's own caller-context by-id read: a principal explaining itself through `recordAbsentToCaller` (absent means no row), an asker explaining another principal through `asker.cannotRead`, which the plugin binds to `unreadableUnderCallerRead` (no row, or a declared 4xx, over the shared `readUnlessRefused`; a store fault propagates and fails the explanation). "Cannot read" routes through the one existing missing-record path (`fetchRecord` answering null), so the record verdict and every layer's `record` are the nonexistent id's; the pins hold whole-decision equality with a nonexistent id, record id set aside, at engine, plugin and REST level. Self versus third party is decided by context identity, and `explainAccessForCaller` keeps `targetContext` as the very `callerContext` object on both self paths (no `userId`, or the caller's own id), so the classification cannot drift between them. No exemption sits beside the door: a system asker is asked and the door returns it the row (pinned).
- **The write arm for an asker who reads a row the explained principal cannot — right.** `principalCannotRead` keeps #22791's `visible: false`; a memoized read-operation pass then yields the principal's READ decider, and `attributeThePrincipalsRead` carries that read's per-record attribution onto each row-scoped layer under a `404 RECORD_NOT_FOUND` preface, so the only status any layer names is the door's 404 (pinned, with the 403 control for a row the principal reads). This satisfies the published `decidedBy` definition (the layer whose `record.outcome` excluded the record), which a write-pass trace cannot: the engine pin where the write composition admits the row and the read excludes it confirms the dev's measurement that one write pass composes none of the read's legs.
- **Ordering and read count — right.** The asker's read precedes the capability and CRUD gates, so a principal refused at the object gate gets, for an unreadable id, exactly what it gets for a nonexistent id (that gate's decider kept, missing-record layers): the ruled invariant. Each (principal, record) pair is read once per explanation (`askedOnce`, `oncePerRecord`), the read pass included; a `create` carrying a `recordId` is asked the asker's read too — one read, nothing disclosed past the door.
- **Spec, `packages/spec/src/security/explain.zod.ts`: description text only — right.** One `.describe()` string on `ExplainDecision.record` and two TSDoc blocks; no schema shape, enum or optionality moves. The sentences match the code: "finds no row for or refuses" for a third-party asker is `unreadableUnderCallerRead`; "finds no row for" for a self-explanation is `absentUnderCallerRead`. The regenerated `content/docs/references/security/explain.mdx` row equals the new string; no `api-surface`, `json-schema.manifest` or `authorable-surface` shard changes, and `check:generated` and `check:docs` ran green inside the required `TypeScript Type Check` job. Precision note, carrier none: "visible false, decidedBy omitted" describes the shape past the object gate; a principal the capability or CRUD gate refuses keeps that gate's decider for an unreadable and a never-existed id alike, which the same sentence's "like a never-existed id" states exactly, and the pre-existing "Missing records" clause carried the same shorthand.
- **Tests touched — right, none weakened.** `explain-enforce-parity.test.ts`: no parity assertion is edited; the rig's explaining administrator gains the explained users' reader set, because under ruling C a refused third-party asker is told the missing record and those cells would stop measuring the explained user's door; the two `single`-posture `record:l_beta` rows join the invariant because the asker's own by-id read is natively scoped to the context organization, and the `readFilter:LEDGER` divergence row stays measured. `explain-cross-class-refusal` and `explain-json-column-refusal` flip the self-explained unreadable read to the whole missing-record answer with load-bearing `toEqual` assertions. `explain-controlled-by-parent-write` re-homes item 1's decider cells on a reading asker and adds the self-explanation and write-arm cells. The dogfood parity pin gains the reading administrator and the batch case beside the GET door.
- **Governed surfaces: none.** None of the 11 paths is under `docs/adr/**`, `docs/NORTH-STAR.md`, `.claude/**`, `skills/**`, `AGENTS.md` or `CLAUDE.md`; `Governed Surface Queue Guard` is `success`; 1125 changed lines, under the 3000-line human-merge threshold. This record is owed for the published-schema face (`explain.zod.ts`), as the seat said.
- **Runtime strings carry no tracker number** (`principalReadPreface`, the `.describe()` text); issue tags sit in code comments only.

### ② Semver level

- `.changeset/22792-explain-asker-gate.md`: `@objectstack/plugin-security: patch` and `@objectstack/spec: patch` — **right.** Both are released packages (`private` unset, at `17.7.0`); the card is `bug`; nothing authorable, exported or accepted moves, so `skip-changeset` does not apply and `minor` is not owed. The spec patch is owed because a published description string and its generated reference page change.
- `Clause-②: no` — **right**, and it stands on all three carriers: PR body line 2, the changeset body, and the claim `6108485513`. No `(widening)` or `(narrowing)` arm, correctly: the accept-set is unchanged and no published type widens or narrows (the dev chose a module-internal entry over an optional key on `ExplainEngineDeps`, so this family's earlier `yes (widening)` precedent is not triggered). Not breaking, so no ADR-0087 disposition marker is owed. `Check Changeset` is `success`.
- Changeset prose against the diff: the "Before" sentences are true of `main` (no asker gate; item 1's decider shown to every asker); "Description text only; no schema shape changes" matches `explain.zod.ts`; "no exported type or signature moves" matches `index.ts` and the exports map.

### ③ Boundary flags

Every flag in the two `os-dev-report`s (`6109766929`, `6112399009`), the PR body's acceptance notes and the seat's ESCALATE and ACCEPT, judged:

1. **Round 1 open question — a refused asker.** Escalated by the seat to decision #22851 and ruled C (`6110031776`); built in round 2 as `unreadableUnderCallerRead` and the `{ context, cannotRead }` asker, with the refused `manage_users` and D12 cells, the edit-only self-explanation CONTROL and the engine classification cells. Answered. Round 2's `open_questions` is empty.
2. **Route: a module-internal entry instead of a per-call `recordAbsentToCaller` binding.** Right — the engine needs both contexts (the by-id write guard and the master leg keep the explained context), and no published type moves.
3. **System-asker exemption removed.** Right — the door returns a system read every row (pinned), and an `isSystem` read site in the engine would be a second notion of "can read".
4. **A second read-operation pass in the write arm.** Right and bounded — only for a third-party asker who reads a row the principal cannot, memoized per explanation.
5. **Interpretive choice: the write arm's layers carry the principal's read attribution under a 404 preface.** Accepted — it is what makes `decidedBy` agree with the layer trace as the spec defines it; the two alternatives the dev names would break either the decider's own layer or the door's status.
6. **Item 1's pending changeset (`22792-explain-read-master-leg.md`) left byte-identical.** Acceptable — unreleased, it ships in the same release as this PR's note, which states the asker qualification and the "Before"; the release-time compiler reads both notes together. Carrier: the seat, at release time. Not a FAIL input.
7. **Drift case not measured as reachable** (the principal's read story admits a row its door withholds): the arm then answers `visible: false` with no decider, the fail-closed direction, and the PR body says so. Accepted.
8. **One more caller-context by-id read per record-grained explanation.** Accepted — the price the ruling sets, once per (principal, record) per explanation.
9. **A principal refused at the object gate gets missing-record layers for an unreadable id.** Right — equal to a nonexistent id, the invariant.
10. **The `explain-enforce-parity` fixture change and the two divergence rows joining the invariant**, which the dev asked the seat to review against its order. Reviewed, right (section ①): no parity assertion weakened; the `readFilter` divergence stays measured.
11. **Process flags** (gates run outside the verify lock per the agent definition; a killed `check:generated --fix` later completed and `check:docs` is green on the head; two merges through `os-regen-merge.sh` with no regeneration owed; a stray pid file outside every repository): none bears on the diff; CI on the head is the gate.
12. **Out-of-scope findings** (the write-arm drift case; the pending-note qualification): carried as noted; by Prime Directive #10's test neither owes a card (no reproducible defect, no contract violation, no authoring trap).
